en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kuraib narrated to us—and the wording is theirs—(H) and Ishaq al-Hanzali narrated to us; Ishaq said: 'Akhbarana' (informed us), and the other two said: 'Haddathana' (narrated to us) Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'No thorn pricks a believer, nor anything above it, but Allah raises him a degree thereby or removes a sin from him.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim both narrated to us from Jarir; Zuhayr said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, who said: Some young men from Quraysh entered upon 'A'ishah while she was in Mina and they were laughing. She said: 'What makes you laugh?' They said: 'So-and-so tripped over the tent rope and his neck or his eye was almost lost.' She said: 'Do not laugh, for indeed I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "No Muslim is pricked by a thorn or anything above it, except that a degree is recorded for him thereby and a sin is erased from him thereby."'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kuraib narrated to us; they said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Yunus and Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Ghaniyyah informed us; all of them from al-A'mash, with the chain of transmission of Jarir, similar to his hadith. And he added in the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah that he said: 'Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, there is no Muslim on earth...'

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; Ishaq said: 'Akhbarana' (informed us), and the other two said: 'Haddathana' (narrated to us) Jarir, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, from 'Abdullah, who said: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) while he was suffering from fever, so I touched him with my hand and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you are suffering from a severe fever.' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Yes, indeed I suffer fever as two men among you suffer fever.' He said: I said: 'Is that because you have a double reward?' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Yes.' Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'No Muslim is afflicted with harm, from illness or anything else, but Allah sheds his sins thereby just as a tree sheds its leaves.' And in the hadith of Zuhayr, 'so I touched him with my hand' is not mentioned.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father informed me; (H) and Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us; they said: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us; (H) and Bishr ibn Khalid narrated to me: Muhammad—meaning Ibn Ja'far—informed us; all of them from Shu'bah, from al-A'mash; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated to me: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us; both of them from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, with the chain of transmission of Jarir, the like of his hadith.

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; Ishaq said: 'Akhbarana' (informed us), and 'Uthman said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from Masruq, who said: 'A'ishah said: 'I never saw any man upon whom pain was more severe than upon the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).' And in the narration of 'Uthman, in place of 'al-waja'u' (the pain), it is 'waja'an' (in pain).

Muhammad ibn Hatim ibn Maymun narrated to me: Bahz narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, will say on the Day of Resurrection: "O son of Adam, I fell ill and you did not visit Me." He will say: "O Lord, how could I visit You when You are the Lord of the worlds?" He will say: "Did you not know that My servant so-and-so fell ill and you did not visit him? Did you not know that if you had visited him, you would have found Me with him? O son of Adam, I asked you for food and you did not feed Me." He will say: "O Lord, how could I feed You when You are the Lord of the worlds?" He will say: "Did you not know that My servant so-and-so asked you for food and you did not feed him? Did you not know that if you had fed him, you would have found that with Me? O son of Adam, I asked you for drink and you did not give Me drink." He will say: "O Lord, how could I give You drink when You are the Lord of the worlds?" He will say: "My servant so-and-so asked you for drink and you did not give him drink; had you given him drink, you would have found that with Me."'
Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to me: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, with this chain of transmission.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb both narrated to us from Yazid—and the wording is Zuhayr's: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: 'Asim al-Ahwal informed us, from 'Abdullah ibn Zayd—who is Abu Qilabah—from Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani, from Abu Asma' al-Rahabi, from Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'Whoever visits a sick person remains in the khurfah of Paradise.' It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the khurfah of Paradise?' He said: 'Its harvested fruits.'

Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us: Khalid narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma' al-Rahabi, from Thawban, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'Indeed, when a Muslim visits his fellow Muslim brother, he remains in the khurfah (harvest) of Paradise until he returns.'

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi narrated to us: Hushaym informed us, from Khalid, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma', from Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Whoever visits a sick person remains in the khurfah (harvest) of Paradise until he returns.'

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Abu al-Rabi' al-Zahrani narrated to us; they said: Hammad—meaning Ibn Zayd—narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma', from Thawban; Abu al-Rabi' said: tracing it back to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and in the hadith of Sa'id he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The visitor of the sick is in the makhrafah (orchard/harvest) of Paradise until he returns.'

The Shaykh Abu Ahmad said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zanjawayh al-Qushayri informed me: 'Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, with this chain of transmission, the like of it.

'Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad narrated to me: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that a man visited a brother of his in another village, so Allah appointed an angel along his path. When he came upon him, he said: 'Where do you intend to go?' He said: 'I intend to visit a brother of mine in this village.' He said: 'Do you owe him any favor that you wish to foster?' He said: 'No, other than that I love him for the sake of Allah, the Exalted and Glorious.' He said: 'Then I am indeed a messenger of Allah to you to inform you that Allah loves you just as you have loved him for His sake.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas, among what was recited to him, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'mar, from Abu al-Hubab Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Indeed, Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection: "Where are those who love one another for My majesty? Today I shall shade them in My shade on the Day when there is no shade except My shade."'

Abu al-Tahir and 'Amr ibn Sawwad narrated to us; they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Malik ibn Anas informed us, from Muslim ibn Abi Maryam, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'The deeds of people are presented every week twice: on Monday and on Thursday, and every believing servant is forgiven except a servant between whom and his brother there is malice, so it is said: "Leave—or delay—these two until they reconcile."'

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Muslim ibn Abi Maryam, from Abu Salih, who heard Abu Hurayrah trace it back once, saying: 'Deeds are presented every Thursday and Monday, and Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, forgives on that day every person who associates nothing with Allah, except a person between whom and his brother there is malice, so it is said: "Delay these two until they make peace; delay these two until they make peace."'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas, among what was recited to him, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The gates of Paradise are opened on Monday and on Thursday, and every servant who does not associate anything with Allah is forgiven, except a man between whom and his brother there is malice, so it is said: "Delay these two until they reconcile; delay these two until they reconcile; delay these two until they reconcile."' Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me: Jarir narrated to us; (H) and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Ahmad ibn 'Abdah al-Dabbi narrated to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Darawardi; both of them from Suhayl, from his father, with the chain of transmission of Malik, similar to his hadith, except that in the hadith of al-Darawardi, in the narration of Ibn 'Abdah, it says: 'except the two who have abandoned each other (al-mutahajirayn),' and Qutaybah said: 'except the two who have forsaken each other (al-muhtajirayn).'

'Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: Kathir ibn Hisham narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Burqan narrated to us, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Indeed, Allah does not look at your appearances or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.'

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Sarh narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from Usamah—who is Ibn Zayd—that he heard Abu Sa'id, the freed slave of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir ibn Kurayz, saying: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said... and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Dawud, adding and omitting, and among what he added in it was: 'Indeed, Allah does not look at your bodies or your appearances, but He looks at your hearts,' and he pointed with his fingers to his chest.

'Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: Dawud—meaning Ibn Qays—narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id, the freed slave of 'Amir ibn Kurayz, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Do not envy one another, do not artificially inflate prices against one another, do not hate one another, do not turn your backs on one another, and do not undercut one another in sales; and be, O servants of Allah, brothers. A Muslim is a brother to a Muslim: he does not wrong him, nor does he let him down, nor does he despise him. Piety is here'—and he pointed to his chest three times—'It is sufficient evil for a person to despise his Muslim brother. All of a Muslim is sacred to a Muslim: his blood, his wealth, and his honor.'

Ahmad ibn Sa'id al-Darimi narrated to me: Habban narrated to us: Wuhayb narrated to us: Suhayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'Do not hate one another, do not turn your backs on one another, do not compete maliciously with one another, and be, O servants of Allah, brothers.'

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani and 'Ali ibn Nasr al-Jahdami narrated to us; they said: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, with this chain of transmission: 'Do not sever ties with one another, do not turn your backs on one another, do not hate one another, do not envy one another, and be brothers as Allah has commanded you.'

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Jarir informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not spy on one another, do not eavesdrop on one another, do not artificially inflate prices against one another, and be, O servants of Allah, brothers.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn Muhammad—narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Do not forsake one another, do not turn your backs on one another, do not eavesdrop on one another, and do not undercut one another in sales; and be, O servants of Allah, brothers.'

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us; he said: I read to Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech. Do not eavesdrop, do not spy, do not compete maliciously, do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not turn your backs on one another, and be, O servants of Allah, brothers.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn Muhammad—narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'There is to be no forsaking beyond three [days].'

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us: al-Dahhak—who is Ibn 'Uthman—informed us, from Nafi', from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'It is not lawful for a believer to forsake his brother for more than three days.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us; they said: Sufyan narrated to us; (H) and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me; (H) and Hajib ibn al-Walid narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Harb narrated to us, from al-Zubaydi; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali, Muhammad ibn Rafi', and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar; all of them from al-Zuhri, with the chain of transmission of Malik and the like of his hadith, except for his saying: 'and this one turns away and that one turns away,' for all of them said in their hadith, unlike Malik: 'and this one averts [his face] and that one averts [his face].'

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us; he said: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Ata' ibn Yazid al-Laythi, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'It is not lawful for a Muslim to forsake his brother for more than three nights, so that when they meet, this one turns away and that one turns away; and the better of the two is the one who initiates the greeting of peace.'
